title: Constant field refinement of a geometrically normal projective curve
statement: Let k be a field and Z an integral projective k-scheme of topological dimension at most one [def-weil-field, def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-kun-projective, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Assume every field base change of Z has integrally closed domain stalks [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. There exist a finite separable field extension L/k [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and a morphism q:Z→Spec L, such that q is smooth, projective and geometrically irreducible [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and q followed by Spec(L)→Spec(k) is the original structure morphism.

source.place: Tag 0GK5, last paragraph; baby Stein factorization

proof.text: Geometric normality in dimension at most one gives smoothness and geometric reducedness.

For the proper integral scheme take L=Γ(Z,O_Z), a field finite over k. Geometric reducedness implies separability. The separable-extension formulation gives a separating transcendence basis for the top intermediate field; finiteness makes this basis empty, yielding ordinary algebraic separability.

The canonical map q:Z→Spec Γ(Z,O_Z) has geometrically connected fibres by affine Stein factorization. Its structure-map factorization is canonical. Finite separable base refinement gives smoothness and projectivity of q.

Use the proved library theorem GeometricallyIrreducible.of_smooth_of_geometricallyConnected: every field fibre is smooth, hence regular, and connected, hence irreducible. Return q and its factorization.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_geonormal_projective_curve_constants
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (Z : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral Z]
    (f : Z ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsHProjective f]
    (hdim : topologicalKrullDim Z ≤ 1)
    (hnormal : ∀ (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L],
      ∀ x : ↥(pullback f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))),
      IsDomain ((pullback f
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).presheaf.stalk x) ∧
      IsIntegrallyClosed ((pullback f
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).presheaf.stalk x)) :
    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L) (q : Z ⟶ Spec (.of L)),
      Module.Finite k L ∧ Algebra.IsSeparable k L ∧ Smooth q ∧ IsHProjective q ∧
      GeometricallyIrreducible q ∧
      q ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)) = f

tool_uses.why: The generic global-functions theorem supplies finiteness and the field structure; the unit has no replacement.
The generic global-functions separability theorem is the constant-field input.
The generic Stein theorem supplies geometric connectedness of the canonical constant-field map.
Smooth fibres over fields are regular in the existing proved library theorem.
Connected regular fibres are irreducible; this generic geometry theorem is not a route around a unit step.
